The Grid Sizes of a Term

Source: R/hyper.R
term_grid.Rd

Reports the number of values that a path visits for each hyperparameter of the term that is swept, one entry per penalty. A hyperparameter that the term holds has no grid and is not reported. A swept hyperparameter for which the term records no size is covered at the default size of the fitting layer.

Usage

term_grid(term, ...)

Arguments

term

A term, built or not.

...

Passed to methods. The shipped methods do not use it.

Value

A named list, one entry per penalty of the term, each a named list of single whole numbers keyed by hyperparameter. The list is empty where the term records no grid size for any hyperparameter.

Details

How finely a hyperparameter is swept belongs to the term because the term is where the penalty is named: a block of four columns and one of four hundred need different grids, and an outer criterion applies to every hyperparameter of the model alike, so a size set there could not distinguish between them.

Only a hyperparameter with a path has a grid, and a held hyperparameter has none. ridge(), s() and te() with their default penalty, and random() with its default Gaussian prior, report nothing, because a marginal criterion estimates their hyperparameters at the mode. A smoother whose penalty factory has a kink is swept by a path but reports nothing either, and the path uses its default size. lasso() reports its n_lambda, enet() reports n_lambda and n_alpha, and scad() and mcp() report n_lambda together with n_a or n_gamma where the shape is estimated, since the shape is held by default. These constructors write their sizes into the term, so lasso(~ x) reports lambda = 25 where an unset argument would give an empty list. A hyperparameter written out as a vector has no grid to build and is not reported here; the path visits the written-out values, which term_values() reports.

The keys are term_penalties()'s entry names, "" for a penalty over the whole term.

See also

term_path_min() for how far down the path reaches, term_search() for how several of them are combined, term_values() for a grid written out instead of counted.

Examples

# A path term reports its grid, at the default and when set.
term_grid(lasso(~ x))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$lambda
#> [1] 25
#> 
#> 
term_grid(lasso(~ x, n_lambda = 50))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$lambda
#> [1] 50
#> 
#> 

# The two axes have two sizes, and the kink axis is swept more finely.
term_grid(enet(~ x))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$lambda
#> [1] 25
#> 
#> [[1]]$alpha
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> 

# A held hyperparameter has no grid, and the held shape of SCAD has none.
term_grid(enet(~ x, alpha = 0.5))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$lambda
#> [1] 25
#> 
#> 
term_grid(scad(~ x))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$lambda
#> [1] 25
#> 
#> 
term_grid(scad(~ x, a = NULL))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$lambda
#> [1] 25
#> 
#> [[1]]$a
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> 

# A penalty with no kink has no path, so there is nothing to count.
term_grid(ridge(~ x))
#> list()
term_grid(s(x, basis7::bspline_smooth(k = 5)))
#> list()
